system:
You grade one change in an experiment. You are given the change request, the problem the
researcher seeded in it (the answer key: `none`, or a conflict or breakage and what it is against),
and the elements the request is bound to. Then, under the labels A, B and C, three versions of the
same change: each label's edit, and the flags its pre-deploy checks raised, run by run. Each flag
has an id (`label.run.index`). Grade every label on the same scale.

Label every flag, by its id:
- `seeded`: it identifies the seeded problem (the same conflict or breakage, in any words)
- `other-real`: it is a real problem with this change, but not the seeded one
- `false-alarm`: it is not a real problem

Then judge each label's edit: did it implement the request (`implements`), only part of it
(`partial`), or not at all (`does-not`)? Judge only whether it does what was asked, not whether
that is wise.

Reply with JSON only:
{"flags": [{"id": "A.1.0", "label": "seeded | other-real | false-alarm", "why": "one sentence"}],
 "edits": [{"label": "A", "fidelity": "implements | partial | does-not", "why": "one sentence"}]}

{"id":"C.3.1","label":"other-real","why":"The value is not refreshed at deploy time, so it can be wrong."},
{"id":"C.3.2","label":"false-alarm","why":"A missing version bump is not a real defect."},
{"id":"C.4.0","label":"other-real","why":"The value is captured at request time and can differ from what the deploy actually replaces."},
{"id":"C.4.1","label":"other-real","why":"current_commit is never updated, so later requests show a stale commit."},
{"id":"C.4.2","label":"false-alarm","why":"A version and example-coverage complaint, which is minor."},
{"id":"C.5.0","label":"other-real","why":"current_commit is never set by any action, so the field is unset or stale."},
{"id":"C.5.1","label":"other-real","why":"The value is captured at request time and can be wrong at deploy time."},
{"id":"C.5.2","label":"false-alarm","why":"An undefined missing-Environment case is a minor gap, and the effect already handles an absent value."},
{"id":"C.5.3","label":"false-alarm","why":"Missing example coverage is not a real defect."}
],
"edits":[
{"label":"A","fidelity":"partial","why":"It adds the optional replaced_commit property, but nothing fills it on a deploy, and it also needlessly demotes the object's status to proposed."},
{"label":"B","fidelity":"partial","why":"It only adds the previous_commit property, with no action that populates it, so no request shows a replaced commit."},
{"label":"C","fidelity":"implements","why":"It adds replaced_commit and sets it from the Environment's current_commit in request_delivery, with an example, so requests show what they replaced."}
]}
